question: The document analysis subagent in your research system has three tools with detailed, well-differentiated descriptions: extract_data_points, summarize_content, and verify_claim_against_source. Logs show that it calls summarize_content for most requests to pull specific figures from a report, even though the extract_data_points description covers exactly this case. The subagent's system prompt contains the instruction "Whenever a request mentions a report, summarize it first." What change would most effectively fix this tool selection problem?

options.text: Merge the three tools into one generic analyze_document tool so the subagent never has to choose among similar tools.
options.reason: The guide recommends splitting generic tools into purpose-specific tools with defined input/output contracts, so merging them goes the wrong way and leaves the prompt problem unfixed.

options.text: Review the system prompt and rewrite the keyword-triggered instruction that pushes the subagent toward summarize_content whenever a report is mentioned.
options.reason: The guide says keyword-sensitive system prompt instructions can create unintended tool associations that override well-written tool descriptions, so the prompt itself must be reviewed and fixed.

options.text: Expand the extract_data_points description with more example queries and edge cases so it wins over the summarize_content tool more often.
options.reason: The descriptions are already clear and differentiated, so the gap is elsewhere: the keyword-sensitive system prompt instruction overrides them, and longer descriptions leave that association in place.

options.text: Set tool_choice to force extract_data_points on every request so the subagent always uses the extraction tool first.
options.reason: Forced tool selection makes every request use extraction, including those that need summaries or claim verification, and it does not remove the keyword-sensitive instruction that causes the misrouting.
